transcript: So, first impressions. I think we, um, overrate how accurate they are and underrate how sticky they are. Research says people decide within seconds whether they trust you, and honestly, that snap judgment colors everything that comes after. If you start strong, small mistakes later get forgiven. If you start badly, you're basically climbing uphill for the rest of the conversation. My opening point is preparation matters most in the first minute, like knowing exactly how you will introduce yourself. The body of my argument is about body language, because posture and eye contact carry more weight than the actual words you choose. To close, I would say treat every first impression as a draft you can revise. People do update their opinions, but only if you give them a clear reason to look twice.
summary: You've structured this thoughtfully with a clear thesis, evidence, and closing—your confidence and pace are genuinely strong. Sharpen the response by replacing hedging words like 'honestly' and 'like' with concrete examples or citations, and you'll elevate this from good to excellent.
